reading.body:
New Hampshire has seven bills touching artificial intelligence or compute recorded through August 2026, and one of them names compute access itself as a legislative subject.

HB1124, titled "Relative to the right to compute," is the outlier that connects most directly to the infrastructure layer underlying AI capability. The other bills address AI use by state agencies, professional licensing, and health-carrier recordkeeping, all of which regulate applications rather than the physical resources that make those applications possible. That one bill frames compute access as something a legislature might protect or restrict is notable, though the data gives no detail on what the bill actually proposes.

The remaining bills cluster around government and professional contexts. SB657 and HB1506 both concern state agency use of AI, suggesting that how government bodies adopt or are restricted from adopting these systems is a live question in New Hampshire. SB640 addresses AI in licensed professions, and HB1406 targets health insurance utilization review, a domain where automated decision-making has drawn scrutiny elsewhere. HB1618, on solar radiation and weather modification, sits outside AI entirely and its presence in this dataset is unexplained by the data given.

What the data does not cover: the status of any bill, whether any passed, failed, or was amended, and what the substantive provisions of HB1124's compute right actually are. The dates run from December 2025 through March 2026, so this is a snapshot of a single legislative session, not a longitudinal trend.
